summary: IDS feed s147_double is degraded: 1.96 Gbps bursts overload 1 Gbps IDS port (8 intervals, 196% capacity) and 63.7% encrypted share exceeds 60% IDS tolerance, both reducing detection coverage.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is delivering bursty aggregated traffic peaking at 1.96 Gbps to a single 1 Gbps IDS port without load-balancing or shaping. 8 intervals exceed 80% utilization threshold, hitting 196% of port capacity.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS ingress buffers overflow and packets are dropped before analysis. IDS misses attacks during bursts, loses flow state (needs both directions and full payload), and detection coverage is incomplete.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute flows across 2x1G IDS ports using flow-aware hashing to keep per-port peaks <0.8 Gbps, preserving both directions per flow for stateful IDS inspection and eliminating drops.

findings.root_cause: 63.66% of bytes are encrypted (TLS/QUIC) vs 60% IDS tolerance. Traffic is forwarded without visibility-layer decryption, so payload is opaque to IDS.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS cannot perform signature, malware or C2 payload inspection on majority of traffic. IDS is effectively blind beyond headers, increasing false negatives despite receiving packets.

recommended_fix.why: Decrypt relevant TLS flows at the visibility layer and forward cleartext to IDS (re-encrypt after if required) to restore full-payload inspection while respecting privacy/compliance via selective policy.
